newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania puts police on alert for Jackson concert.
newsitem.headline: Romania puts police on alert for Jackson concert.

text.p: Post-communist Romania, unused to pop hysteria, put police on alert for Michael Jackson's concert in Bucharest on Saturday.
More than 70,000 fans cheered Jackson as he popped out of a space capsule in Bucharest's National Stadium for a two-hour performance on the third leg of his "HIStory World Tour".
Local fans scrambled for tickets on sale for $30 dollars, a small fortune in the impoverished Balkan country, but fans from Japan, Germany and the Netherlands also flew in for the show.
"He's my king, he's the greatest," said Louisa Verhulsdonk, one of a group of Dutch fans who also attended Jackson's previous concerts in Prague and Budapest.
Jackson, 38, picked Eastern Europe to launch his first tour in three years, seen as a bid to put his career back on track after allegations of child molestation.

Romania, little used to celebrity visits, put police on top alert for the concert, but no incidents were recorded. Nurses staffing medical tents at the stadium danced with the crowds as Jackson displayed his singing and dancing skills.
Unlike on his last visit in 1992, to launch his "Dangerous" tour, Jackson was not courted by politicians.

He played with children in two Bucharest orphanages on Friday, confronting head-on the scandal that erupted around him in 1993, when a 13-year-old boy accused the singer of molesting him. Jackson denied wrongdoing but reached a multi-million dollar out-of-court settlement.
"He's great and he cares about us," said Anca Verdes, 15, echoing one of Jackson's previous hits. "Nobody cares about us," she added as she was dazzled by the fireworks, lasers and pyrotechnics.
Moscow is the next leg of the tour, which will take hundreds of tonnes of equipment to stops in Europe, Africa and Asia over the next three months. No dates have been scheduled for the Americas.
